first_impression.reaction: Googled 'mykonos wedding venues' because Mykonos is one of the islands we're weighing up and I'm comparing three planners. The intro sorts the island by area and says it comes down to guest count, ceremony and how guests get around. That's criteria, not 'paradise'. Went to the FAQ first, then the table, which admits its blanks. Read the venues big enough for our list, the weather bit and the legal section properly. The numbers mostly hang together when I check them against each other. Two places where the page joins dots it hasn't earned: the legal-marriage logic around Lolita's 'civil' weddings, and ZeNIT going ahead 'in any weather'.

journey.quote: The right one depends on how many guests you are inviting, the ceremony you want and how your guests will move around the island.

journey.section: Mykonos wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: No made-up 'number one', and the gaps are admitted. Half the table says 'Not published' and I trust it more for that.

journey.section: Mykonos wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: When you have three or four names, book a Wedded Concierge consultation to see which are free on your dates.
journey.reaction: A booking link straight after the table, before I've read a single venue. At least it says 'when you have three or four names' and not 'book now'. Minor.

journey.quote: Mykonos Blu is the only venue here that publishes a room count.
journey.reaction: Says outright that the page runs out of data, and tells me what to ask. Rooms are what we'd actually need for long-haul guests, so that matters to me.

journey.section: Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: The hotel's rule is that both bride and groom must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: That's the catch with this one, and it's on the page, in the table and in the FAQ. Good. Most sites would show me the chapel photo and leave this out.

journey.section: Saint John Hotel Villas & Spa, Agios Ioannis
journey.quote: The hotel works with wedding planners for flowers, candles, DJs, photography, video and fireworks, at additional charge.
journey.reaction: 'At additional charge' is the bit I'm always looking for. Tells me the 800-guest headline isn't all-in.

journey.section: Petasos Beach Resort & Spa, Platis Gialos
journey.quote: The Swimming Pool takes 280 for a banquet, 350 for a reception and 500 for cocktails; the V.I.P. Restaurant 180, 220 and 300; Le Club Restaurant 70, 90 and 110.
journey.reaction: Numbers per space per layout. This is what I'd put in a spreadsheet. And it admits the ceremony venue isn't published, rather than guessing.

journey.section: Royal Myconian and Myconian Imperial, Elia
journey.quote: The kitchens are certified halal and kosher, and a South Asian chef cooks traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Specific and checkable. Half our guests would care about this more than the view.

journey.quote: This is the only venue on the list that names civil weddings at its chapel, which matters if you want the legal ceremony and the setting in one place.
journey.reaction: Hang on. A hotel's wedding page saying 'civil' isn't the same as the legal marriage being done at that chapel. Who officiates? Is it legally registered in Greece? The legal section further down doesn't connect the two either. This is the page drawing a conclusion the source doesn't give it.

journey.section: ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: A 20 m infinity pool facing the sea and Delos, two cocktail bars, an open-view kitchen and a central indoor hall, so the celebration can go ahead in any weather.
journey.reaction: 'Any weather' for a venue whose capacity is 'not published'. I don't know if the indoor hall holds the whole guest list, so I can't take 'any weather' at face value. It's the page's claim, not the venue's numbers.

journey.section: ZeNIT Events Center, above Paradise beach
journey.quote: The venue's own services include a physician and medical room during events, security with CCTV, and guest transfers that ZeNIT runs itself for up to 16 guests, with larger groups handled through its partners and transfers by sea also offered.
journey.reaction: Boring, practical, with a number and a limit. That's the good kind.

journey.quote: If your guest list is larger than a chapel holds, many couples keep the ceremony small and gather everyone for the reception that follows.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' on what basis? Harmless advice, but it's the one line in the section with nothing behind it.

journey.quote: Wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer, from June to September, including near tourist areas, and can start with little warning and travel quickly.
journey.reaction: Dated, linked to Smartraveller, not buried. Most wedding sites would leave the wildfires out.

journey.quote: A date outside the summer months sits outside the heatwave and wildfire season.
journey.reaction: Fine, but which months? There's no temperature, wind or rainfall figure for May, June or October anywhere. On 'the island of the winds' I'd want an actual number before I picked a date.

journey.quote: All notarial services need an appointment, though apostille and CNI documents can be sent by post, and legalised documents and CNIs are ready within two working days.
journey.reaction: Specific, linked to the Embassy, and says what they won't do. Good.

journey.quote: Yes. Grecotel Mykonos Lolita, for one, lists civil weddings at its chapel.
journey.reaction: Same jump again, and this time it's the evidence for 'can Australians legally get married here'. A hotel marketing page is the weakest possible answer to a legal question. The Smartraveller sentence after it is the real answer. Lead with that.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't say whether any of these venues pay you as well.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and does that affect which ones the Wedded Advisor recommends?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what does it cover?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I come away with?
Is a 'civil' wedding at Grecotel Mykonos Lolita's chapel a legally registered Greek marriage, and who officiates it?
Does ZeNIT's central indoor hall hold a full guest list if the weather turns?
What are the typical temperatures and wind in May, June, September and October on Mykonos?
Is there a real Mykonos wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: Yes. Grecotel Mykonos Lolita, for one, lists civil weddings at its chapel.
turn_offs_found.why: It answers a legal question with a hotel's marketing wording. 'Lists civil weddings' doesn't prove the marriage is legally registered there, and the body repeats the same leap ('the legal ceremony and the setting in one place'). If the page stretches here, I start rechecking everything else.

turn_offs_found.quote: A 20 m infinity pool facing the sea and Delos, two cocktail bars, an open-view kitchen and a central indoor hall, so the celebration can go ahead in any weather.
turn_offs_found.why: The same entry says capacity isn't published, so nothing on the page shows the indoor hall fits everyone. 'Any weather' is a promise the numbers don't back.

turn_offs_found.quote: When you have three or four names, book a Wedded Concierge consultation to see which are free on your dates.
turn_offs_found.why: It comes straight after the table, before any venue has been described. The wording is soft and conditional, so it's minor, but the pitch still comes before the proof.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the comparison table and the chapel rules (the Christian Orthodox catch at Mykonos Grand)
My dad, the wildfire and heat paragraphs and the CNI and Embassy section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The page mostly earned it: honest blanks, catches named (Orthodox-only religious weddings, 'at additional charge', Katikies' child policy), per-space capacities, sourced and dated risks. What holds me back is the legal-marriage leap from a hotel page and the 'any weather' line, so I'd double-check those before trusting the rest. And I still don't know whether you take a cut from the venues.

top_3_changes: Fix the legal-marriage leap (must-fix): in the FAQ 'Can Australians legally get married in Mykonos?' lead with the Smartraveller CNI and recognition facts, not Lolita's 'civil' wording, and in the Lolita entry drop or soften 'which matters if you want the legal ceremony and the setting in one place' unless the venue says the civil ceremony is legally registered there. Add 'is a civil ceremony here legally registered, and who officiates?' as an ask.

Soften ZeNIT's 'so the celebration can go ahead in any weather' to what the venue publishes (a central indoor hall), and add 'ask whether the hall holds your full guest list' given capacity isn't published. Also drop or soften the unbacked 'many couples' line in 'Where the chapels are'.

Optionally move the first Concierge link below the first venue section, and if a sourced figure exists, give shoulder-season temperature or wind numbers for the 'outside the summer months' advice. (Commission and fee-model detail would also help, but that's a deferred business detail, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, cross-checked claims against each other, looked for catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; fee, commission and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: The Lolita 'civil weddings' -> legal marriage inference appears in the venue entry and as the lead evidence in the legal FAQ. Is it a writer fix this round (reword to what the venue states, lead the FAQ with Smartraveller), or does the source pack confirm that civil ceremonies at the chapel are legally registered?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'mykonos wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Mykonos is one live option among several, hence relevance 4 rather than 5.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
Venue wording in quotation marks (e.g. 'experts in romance and discretion') is clearly attributed to the venue, so it is not counted as the brand's own unsupported claim.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not flagged.
